title: Signal catalog & oncall rehydration playbook
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a pragmatic playbook for observability signals and oncall actions specifically focused on cache rehydration / session rehydrate events (what we call "rehydration windows"). It stitches metric definitions, tracing anchors, dashboard layouts, and short investigation recipes so oncall can make fast, consistent decisions during incidents where cold prefixes / KV-eviction behavior cause latency or cost spikes.

Scope and motivation:
- Target: inference serving (tokenized generation + chat) where prefix/KV cache and request batching interact to produce transient latency spikes.
- Why separate playbook: many existing obs docs cover SLOs and generic probes; rehydration events have unique signal correlations (prefix hit-rates, kv-miss tail, token-first-latency vs TTFB) that need explicit mapping.
- Goal: 5–10 minute triage to either (a) identify and narrow to tenant/capacity layer, (b) apply a mitigation (route to warm variant, temporarily increase batch timeout), or (c) trigger fast rollback / failover.

Key concept: Rehydration Index (RI)
- Definition: RI = weighted sum(instant_kv_miss_rate * 0.6, cold_prefix_pct * 0.3, first_token_latency_p50_normalized * 0.1) normalized 0..100.
- Why: single-number early-warning for emergent cold-cache effects that correlate to token-first-latency spikes and cost surge.
- Implementation notes: compute in metrics tier as a derived timeseries using 10s windows; expose both raw components and RI for dashboards/alerts.

Canonical metric definitions (operator-facing):
- request.count: count of inference requests served (per-tenant, per-model, per-route).
- tokens.generated: number of output tokens produced (per-request aggregated).
- kv.prefetch.hit_rate: percentage of KV lookups served from local cache within 1ms.
- kv.eviction.rate: evictions per minute per pool.
- prefix.cold_pct: percent of requests that hit a cold prefix (no cached KV entries).
- first_token.latency.p50|p95: time from request start to first token emitted.
- tail.token.latency.p99: end-to-end latency for token emission at p99.
- rehydration.index: derived metric described above.
- route.fallback.count: number of requests routed to fallback model/region.
- batch.size.avg: average batch size during 1m window.
- burst.enqueue_queue_length: instantaneous queue length caused by burst throttling.

Tracing & span conventions (quick reference):
- Root span: inference.request (attributes: tenant_id, route, model, seq_len, debug_flag).
- Child spans (recommended order):
  - runtime.kv.lookup (attr: kv_pool, lookup_count, hit=true|false)
  - runtime.kv.prefetch (attr: bytes_prefetched, preshifted=true|false)
  - runtime.batch.coalesce (attr: batch_id, batch_size)
  - runtime.kernel.exec (attr: device, kernel_name, seq_len)
  - runtime.stream.emit (attr: first_token_time)
- Important: add span tag "rehydration.anchor" when prefix.cold_pct>0.2 for the request so trace sampling can prioritize correlated traces.
- Sampling rule: sample 100% of traces where rehydration.index > 70 AND first_token.latency.p95 > baseline*1.5; otherwise probabilistic sampling (0.2%).

Dashboard composition (operator-first):
- Top row: RI time-series (global + per-pool), request.count, tokens.generated.
- Heatmap row: per-tenant prefix.cold_pct heatmap + kv.prefetch.hit_rate. Highlight top 10 tenants by RI.
- Latency row: first_token p50/p95/p99 per-model with anomaly shading.
- Capacity row: batch.size.avg, kv.eviction.rate, device_utilization (%).
- Investigator pane (hidden by default): span-linked sample traces, top slow traces, recent rollout changelog (linked).
- Quick-actions widget: toggle to reroute traffic to warm variant (ops only), temporarily bump prefetch budget for a pool, or mute noisy tenant alerts.

Alerts & thresholds (heuristic starter set):
- RI > 60 for 3m (page oncall)
- first_token.p95 > baseline*2 for 5m (page)
- kv.prefetch.hit_rate drop > 30% vs baseline for 10m (notify)
- kv.eviction.rate spike > 5x baseline (notify)
Notes: these are intentionally conservative; pair each alert with a runbook link and suggested mitigation steps.

Probe design and cadence:
- Synthetic probe type A (prefix-warm): every 30s per-pool, issue short prompt with known prefix to measure TTFB and KV hit (should be warm).
- Synthetic probe type B (prefetch-stress): every 5m, simulate mix of long-tail prefixes to probe eviction behavior; low sampling across tenants to control cost.
- Annealing: on suspected rehydration incidents, temporarily increase probe density in affected pool for 15m then decay back to baseline.

Oncall investigation checklist (5–10 minute flow):
1) Confirm the alert and scope: look at RI, top tenants, per-pool heatmap (1m).
2) Correlate with batch.size.avg and kv.eviction.rate. If eviction spike -> capacity/appliance pressure.
3) Open trace samples (click RI spike) and inspect runtime.kv.lookup hits/misses and batch.coalesce sizes.
4) If many cold prefixes but low eviction.rate -> recent rollout or model variant pinning issue. Check rollout log widget.
5) Mitigate: route affected tenant to warm model or increase prefetch budget on pool; if unknown, shift small percentage (canary) via routing control.
6) If mitigation reduces RI and first_token.latency -> move to postmortem. If not, escalate to infra/serving-runtime.

Ownership & signal stewardship:
- Metric owners: prefix.cold_pct, kv.prefetch.hit_rate, kv.eviction.rate -> eng-serving-runtime
- RI, dashboard, alerts -> eng-observability (oncall and dashboard owners)
- Tracing schema and sampling -> eng-instrumentation
- Probe harness -> eng-operational-scripts (ops-runbooks)

Implementation notes & caveats:
- RI is a band-aid; do not fold all paging decisions solely on RI. Always inspect raw components.
- Derived metrics must survive counter resets; use rolling-window aggregation logic at ingestion time.
- Avoid per-request heavy attribute tagging in high-traffic paths; instead emit lightweight counters and attach heavier metadata only on sampled traces.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Tune RI weights with historical incidents (action item: run regression on last 6 incidents by Feb 2026).
- Decide threshold gating for 100% trace sampling — maybe reserve for incidents only (cost cap).
- Determine how to surface tenant cost impact w/ RI (linked to billing) — exploratory spike card.

Notes to self / quick ideas (informal):
- Consider adding a "rehydration run-length" metric: how long it takes for a tenant to return to warm-hit baseline after eviction event. Handy for SRE capacity math.
- Would be neat to show a "prefix-resonance" map: prefixes that cause disproportionate KV churn. Might come later as a weekly offline job.
- Keep the investigator pane minimal — oncall burnout if we surface too many widgets.

References and links:
- CONFLUENCE-OBS-4521: rehydration experiments notebook
- JIRA-OPS-1198: probe-harness work item
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/332 (RI prototype)
